records.rule: For managed multi-stage work use a deterministic named session and explicit allocate -> stage -> install -> execute -> retrieve -> stop lifecycle.
The installed CLI version and subcommand help are the runtime authority. Probe before emitting optional flags; current upstream main may differ from a pinned 0.6.0 installation.
For the qualified CLI 0.6.0 incident, repair KernelClient in the exact CLI Python environment and prove the fix with a secret-free probe; do not universalize the pin.
Requested accelerator is not observed capacity. Verify actual GPU identity, CUDA-visible memory, host total/available RAM and disk in the worker before expensive work.

As of 2026-09-02 current upstream main advertises GPU T4/L4/G4/H100/A100 and TPU v5e1/v6e1, but availability is entitlement/capacity dependent. Treat the installed help and successful allocation plus worker observation as authority for a given run.
Carry secret references separately from ordinary job environment; never place bearer values in argv, generated source, logs or manifests; retire staged secrets on every terminal path.
Retry only classified transient transport loss in the same live session with bounded backoff; fail fast on deterministic package/dependency errors.
Verify and compact large artifacts locally; upload only required immutable digest-bound payloads. One failed 480 MB transfer is not evidence of a universal size limit.
Use exec -f for local code; feature-detect environment flags. Ordinary non-secret configuration may be materialized in a driver when necessary, but secrets stay on a separate plane.
Report the lifecycle stage that failed. Training success, infrastructure success and promotion success are separate facts.
Treat the runtime filesystem as ephemeral; retrieve and verify durable output artifacts before stop.
Keep local Colab API authentication, optional VM/GCP authentication, and workload/model credentials as separate authority planes.
Stop the session and retire secrets on every terminal path. Cleanup success is evidence of cleanup, not evidence that the job itself succeeded.
